subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram Channel: Support Thread Binding for Subagent Sessions

question: Should Telegram expose child-topic native subagent session spawning now, and should that be implemented through the active per-kind capability/adapter design while keeping ordinary Telegram top-level placement as current?
rationale: Current main has generic adapter-based binding and Telegram current-conversation binding, but the remaining behavior affects visible Telegram topic creation, model-visible spawn capability, plugin API shape, and session/message routing defaults.

options.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review findings, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

options.title: Defer child-topic spawning
options.body: Keep Telegram current-conversation binding only and leave this issue open until maintainers settle the user-visible topic and API model.

options.title: Reject child-topic subagent spawning
options.body: Close this issue and associated candidate PRs if maintainers decide internal subagent work should not create Telegram topics.

recommendation.title: Review or replace the active Telegram PR
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82023 as the main design input, resolve conflicts and review findings, and require final-head live Telegram proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger authored the current core thread-binding refactor and is the strongest history signal for the policy/API decision.
